title: factory settings
description: agentbay.config.yaml modes.factory. The pipeline, the review lenses, the slice constraints and the language profile are settings, so a project changes the factory's workflow without touching the mode. A list setting is replaced whole, never merged entry by entry.

language.description: The language profile the run builds in: a file languages/<name>.yaml of the factory component (python, typescript, go). It names the file globs, the check commands and the practices every builder is held to.

pipeline.description: The stages of a run, in order. Each is one endpoint of this mode; dropping an entry drops that stage, and reordering them reorders the run.

parallel.description: how many of this stage's calls may be out at once; the stage fans out to at most this many slices (build, fix, integrate) or slice-lens pairs (audit)

lenses.description: audit only: the lens ids to run (default: every lens in `reviewers`)

maxRounds.description: fix only: how many fix rounds one slice may have before the run reports it blocked for the owner

reviewers.description: The review lenses. Every lens reviews every slice, in its own call, so the lenses run in parallel and one lens's verdict never hides another's. A lens's checks are ids the reviewer must return a verdict for, next to the slice's own acceptance criteria.

default.title: Correctness
focus: the acceptance criteria, each against the code and the tests that show it
what the tests do not cover

checks.statement: Every acceptance criterion is met by the code, and the evidence names the file and line or the command and its output.
The slice has a test for each criterion that can be tested, and the tests fail without the change.
Error paths and edge cases the criteria imply are handled, not left to crash.

default.title: Structure and boundaries
focus: the slice's boundary: only its own paths changed
the interfaces at its edges, exactly as the brief states them

checks.statement: Nothing outside the slice's declared paths was changed.
Every interface the slice publishes matches the shape in the brief, and every one it consumes is used as stated.
No module reaches around a published interface into another slice's internals.
Names, layering and file placement follow the conventions already in the codebase.

default.title: Quality and readability
focus: the practices of the language profile

checks.statement: No commented-out code, debug output, placeholder or TODO stands in for work the criteria require.
The change adds no duplication an existing helper already covers.
Every practice of the language profile in the brief is followed, or the departure is explained in the result.

default.title: Performance and resources
focus: work per call and per item
queries, allocations and I/O in loops

checks.statement: No query, request or file read sits inside a loop that could do it once.
The cost of the hot path is stated in terms of the input size, and nothing in it is worse than the plan assumed.
Nothing holds the whole input in memory where a stream or a batch would do.

default.title: Security and data handling
focus: untrusted input at the slice's edges
what the slice logs or returns

checks.statement: No secret, token or credential is in the code, the tests, the output or the logs.
Input that crosses the slice's edge is validated or escaped before it reaches a query, a command, a path or a template.
Errors and logs say what failed without repeating personal data or request bodies.

tier.description: reported in the brief; the step's own tier is set in mode.yaml

blocking.description: false: this lens's fails are recorded and fixed, but never hold a slice out of integration

ignores.description: what this lens leaves to another lens, so two reviewers do not report the same finding

constraints.description: What a slicing must satisfy. `factory.slices/v1.propose` refuses a slicing that breaks one of these and names the slice and the rule, so the slicing is fixed before anything is built.

maxAcceptance.description: acceptance criteria one slice may declare; more than this means the slice is too big

requireInterfaces.description: a slice with a dependency, or one another slice depends on, must declare the interface at that edge

disjointPaths.description: two slices of the same wave may not declare the same path, so parallel builders never write the same file

forbiddenPaths.description: path prefixes no slice may declare, whatever the plan says

maxFixRounds.description: fix rounds one slice may have before the run reports it blocked

worktreeRoot.description: Where the slice worktrees are cut, relative to the project. It must stay inside the path the build env may write.

branchPrefix.description: The run's integration branch is <prefix><runId>, and a slice's branch is <prefix><runId>/<sliceId>. The factory never commits to a branch outside this prefix.
